safety_lead_time.comparison_action: decrease SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 2.17 days

narrative: Material PL1__MD2C777C exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=0.21) with a mean of 1,942 units/day across 209 working days. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.57, mean=2.23 days), and this lead-time uncertainty accounts for 94.4% of the required safety stock. The previous SAP policy carried zero safety stock and ordered only at the MOQ of 73 units, generating ~6,650 orders/year and near-zero holding costs but enormous ordering costs. The optimized (r,Q) policy sets an EOQ-based order quantity of 6,433 units (~75 orders/year) and a safety stock of 4,218 units to achieve the 95% service level target, reducing total annual costs by 96.2%.
warnings: Storage utilization post-replenishment: 10,651 / 12,057 units (88.3%) — approaching capacity; monitor for demand spikes.
Lead time CV=0.57 is highly variable; 94.4% of safety stock is driven by lead time uncertainty — supplier reliability improvement recommended.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous (100% non-zero working days), moderate in variability, and high in volume. The (r,Q) policy is theoretically optimal under these conditions, balancing ordering and holding costs via EOQ while the reorder point absorbs demand and lead-time uncertainty. The MOQ of 73 is non-binding (EOQ=6,433 >> MOQ), so EOQ drives the order quantity directly.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Post-replenishment inventory (SS=4,218 + OQ=6,433 = 10,651 units) reaches 88.3% of the 12,057-unit storage cap. The capacity constraint is not currently binding, but a demand surge causing a higher safety stock recommendation could push against the cap. Recommend monitoring quarterly.
